title: DOAH 26-0133PIC Order: AND MARIA MATOS vs. CORPORATION
text:
STATE OF FLORIDA
DIVISION OF ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS
FRANCISCO MATOS
AND MARIA MATOS,
Petitioners,
vs. Case No. 26-0133PIC
CITIZENS PROPERTY INSURANCE
CORPORATION,
Respondent.
/
ARBITRATION AWARD
Petitioners, who are insured by Respondent Citizens Property Insurance
Corporation ("Citizens"), submitted an insurance claim for a date of loss of
July 8, 2025. Citizens assigned it claim number 001-00-611471. After
Citizens denied the claim at least to some degree, Petitioners disputed that
claim determination, and Citizens demanded in January 2026 that the
dispute be arbitrated at the Division of Administrative Hearings. The matter
was assigned to the undersigned and an arbitration hearing was scheduled
for 9:00 a.m., on March 25, 2026, via Zoom.1
Petitioners did not appear at the arbitration hearing. Citizens was
present. The arbitrator waited until 9:15 a.m., and, with no appearance by
Petitioners or their counsel, the arbitrator adjourned the hearing.
1 This is an arbitration, not a chapter 120 administrative proceeding or a civil action. By the
parties' agreement and the operation of law, this arbitration is mandatory, binding, and
irrevocable. Prados v. Citizens Prop. Ins. Corp., Case No. 24-3731 (Fla. DOAH Mar. 17,
2025); §§ 682.013(1), 682.02(1), Fla. Stat.

Because Petitioners did not introduce evidence at the arbitration hearing,
they did not meet their initial burden of proof in this matter, which is to
prove that their dwelling suffered a direct physical loss during the policy
period.2 Empire Pro Restoration, Inc. v. Citizens Prop. Ins. Corp., 322 So. 3d
96, 98 (Fla. 4th DCA 2021); Mejia v. Citizens Prop. Ins. Corp., 161 So. 3d 576,
578 (Fla. 2d DCA 2014). Accordingly, Petitioners' loss is not covered by the
Citizens policy and the amount of policy benefits payable on this insurance
claim is zero dollars.
DONE AND ORDERED this 25th day of March, 2026, in Tallahassee,
Leon County, Florida.
